title: Change a user's password using the command line
summary: Use the `pwpolicy` command to set a new password for a specific user account. This requires administrator privileges.

aliases.text: change password via command line mac

steps.explain: Run the pwpolicy command with sudo to set a new password for the specified user. You will be prompted for your administrator password first.

placeholders.name: AUTHENTICATOR
placeholders.description: The authentication method, often 'local' or similar depending on setup

placeholders.name: USERNAME
placeholders.description: The short name of the user account (e.g., 'john')

placeholders.name: NEW_PASSWORD
placeholders.description: The new password you want to set

rollback.explain: There is no direct command to revert a password change. You must set it back to the previous value using the same command if you know the old password, or reset it via System Settings.

warnings: This command changes the password immediately. Ensure you have the new password saved.
Incorrect usage can lock you out of the account if you do not have admin access.
